provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Things in the home
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list things in the home.
The pupils should be able to sort home things.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about our school.
Today we learn about things in our homes.
Content:
Things in the home are chairs, cups, spoons.
Chairs are for sitting.
Cups are for drinking water.
Spoons are for eating food.
We sort things by putting them together.
Put all cups here.
Put all chairs there.
Class activity:
We will play a sorting game.
I will show you things.
You will put them in the right place.
Evaluation questions:
Name three things in your home.
What do we use a spoon for?
Show me where cups go.
Summary:
We learned about things in the home.
We can sort them by what they do.

topics.title: Jobs at home
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name jobs at home.
The pupils should be able to explain how to help at home.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about things in the home.
Today we learn about jobs we do at home.
Content:
Jobs at home are sweeping and washing.
Sweeping means cleaning the floor.
Washing means cleaning dishes or clothes.
We help our parents at home.
We sweep when the floor is dirty.
We wash when dishes are dirty.
Class activity:
We will pretend to sweep and wash.
First we sweep with our hands.
Then we wash with our arms.
Evaluation questions:
What is sweeping?
What do we wash at home?
How do you help at home?
Summary:
We learned about jobs at home.
We can help our parents.

topics.title: The work of mummy and daddy
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state what mummy and daddy do.
The pupils should be able to name different jobs.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about jobs at home.
Today we learn about the work of mummy and daddy.
Content:
Mummy and daddy work to get money.
Mummy may cook food for the family.
Daddy may build houses or fix things.
Some mummies are teachers.
Some daddies sell things at the market.
They work hard to buy food for us.
Class activity:
We will play a game called my parent's job.
Each pupil will say what their parent does.
We will clap for each job.
Evaluation questions:
What does your mummy do?
What does your daddy do?
Why do parents work?
Summary:
Mummy and daddy work for us.
We should thank them for their work.

topics.title: Tools in the kitchen
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name kitchen tools.
The pupils should be able to sort kitchen tools.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about parent's work.
Today we learn about tools in the kitchen.
Content:
Tools in the kitchen are spoon, pot, cup.
A spoon is for eating food.
A pot is for cooking food.
A cup is for drinking water.
We sort tools by what they do.
Put all eating tools here.
Put all cooking tools there.
Class activity:
We will play kitchen tool sorting.
I will show you pictures of tools.
You will sort them into groups.
Evaluation questions:
Name three kitchen tools.
What do we use a pot for?
Show me the eating tools.
Summary:
We learned about kitchen tools.
We can sort them by what they do.

topics.title: Planting a seed
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain how to plant a seed.
The pupils should be able to plant a maize seed.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about kitchen tools.
Today we learn how to plant a seed.
Content:
Planting a seed means putting it in soil.
We use maize seeds for planting.
First we dig a small hole in the soil.
Then we put one seed in the hole.
We cover the seed with soil.
Class activity:
We will plant maize seeds in cups.
Each pupil will get a cup with soil.
We will put one seed in each cup.
We will cover the seed with soil.
Evaluation questions:
What do we plant in soil?
How do we cover the seed?
What do seeds need to grow?
Summary:
We learned how to plant a seed.
We planted maize seeds in cups.

topics.title: Caring for plants
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name ways to care for plants.
The pupils should be able to water a plant.
Introduction:
Last week we planted maize seeds.
Today we learn how to care for plants.
Content:
Caring for plants means watering them.\ Plants need water to grow.
We water plants every day.
We watch plants to see them grow.
If a plant looks dry we water it.
Plants need sunlight too.
Class activity:
We will water our planted seeds.
Each pupil will get a small cup of water.
We will pour water on our seeds.
We will watch for changes.
Evaluation questions:
How often do we water plants?
What happens when plants get water?
What else do plants need?
Summary:
We learned how to care for plants.
We watered our seeds.

topics.title: Animals at home
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name animals at home.
The pupils should be able to explain how to feed animals.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about caring for plants.
Today we learn about animals at home.
Content:
Animals at home are fowl, goat, cat.
A fowl says cock-a-doodle-doo.
A goat says baa baa.
A cat says meow meow.
We feed animals every day.
We give fowl maize to eat.
We give goat grass to eat.
We give cat fish to eat.
Class activity:
We will play animal feeding game.
Each pupil will be an animal.
We will pretend to feed each animal.
Evaluation questions:
Name three animals at home.
What does a fowl say?
What do we give a goat to eat?
Summary:
We learned about animals at home.
We know how to feed them.

topics.title: Food we eat
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name foods we eat.
The pupils should be able to sort foods.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about animals at home.
Today we learn about the food we eat.
Content:
Food we eat are rice, beans, yam.
Rice is white and soft.
Beans are small and brown.
Yam is hard and white inside.
We eat food to grow strong.
We sort food by what they are.
Put all grains here.
Put all roots there.
Class activity:
We will play food sorting game.
I will show you pictures of food.
You will sort them into groups.
Evaluation questions:
Name three foods we eat.
What color is rice?
Where do beans come from?
Summary:
We learned about food we eat.
We can sort them by what they are.

topics.title: Keeping the compound clean
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain how to keep compound clean.
The pupils should be able to pick papers and sweep.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about food we eat.
Today we learn how to keep our compound clean.
Content:
Keeping compound clean means no dirt.
We pick papers on the ground.
We sweep the compound every day.
We work together to keep it clean.
When we see trash we put it in bin.
A clean compound is healthy for us.
Class activity:
We will pretend to clean compound.
First we pick papers from floor.
Then we sweep with brooms.
We work together like a team.
Evaluation questions:
How do we keep compound clean?
What do we do with papers on ground?
Why is clean compound good?
Summary:
We learned how to keep compound clean.
We can work together to do it.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to answer questions about term work.
The pupils should be able to name things learned this term.
Introduction:
This week we will revise what we learned.
We will play games to remember.
Content:
We learned about things in home.
We learned about jobs at home.
We learned about parent's work.
We learned about kitchen tools.
We learned about planting seeds.
We learned about caring for plants.
We learned about animals at home.
We learned about food we eat.
We learned about keeping compound clean.
Class activity:
We will play revision games.
First we name things in home.
Then we say jobs at home.
We clap for each correct answer.
Evaluation questions:
Name three things in home.
What do we use a pot for?
How do we care for plants?
Name three animals at home.
What food do you like?
Summary:
We revised all we learned this term.
We are ready for next term.
